name: Mokati
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Pick 2020 'A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon' (UH diss, hdl 10125/73354): Mokati section (3.3) has no stress statement
earlier_scan.note: Pick 2020 covers Mokati phonemes/morphology but explicitly no stress data

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: OLAC 'Resources in and about the Wanambre language' (wnb), Internet Archive copy up-to-date as of 2025-11-04
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists only PARADISEC JZ2 tapes (JZ2-493, -520, -521, -F12 'Lg F12 Wanambre Word List and Vocabulary'), Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, Ethnologue, Z'graggen 1980; no language description exists.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 485 pp. (ScholarSpace hdl 10125/73354)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.3 Mokati (pp. 111-118; author's own 2016/2018 fieldwork + Z'graggen wordlist/tapes): consonant phonemes, Tinami vs Wanambre dialect TAM suffixes, morphophonology -- nothing on stress. Sec. 1.5.1 'Stress' (pp. 31-32): stress described only for Mauwake, Pamosu, Usan; 'Unfortunately, the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Wanambre language' (stub citing Ethnologue and Pick 2020)
sources.note: Nothing; dialect note only (Wanambre/Mawet vs Tinami/Kotakot).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU. (Wanambre = F12)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Intro sec. 7 (pp. viii-ix): transcription 'semi-phonemic', fluctuation table lists Wanambre l~r; nothing on stress; F12 forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check of printed p. 20). p. vii: Capell's 1952 'Vanembere' list represents Musar, not Wanambre.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975a. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, Pacific Linguistics C-38: 569-612.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification and comparative pronoun/lexical rows (F12 Wanambre); nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975b. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Gazetteer/map volume; F12 Wanambre listed; no phonology.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Wanambre = language 30, Mawamuan Family)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 1.3.3 p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Sec. 2.22.23.3 p. 53 Mawamuan typology: segmental/morphological notes only (/h/, l/r contrast in Wanambre, prenasalised voiced stops, preposed negation). Sec. 2.22.8 p. 73 (Adelbert Range Phylum): 'None of the languages appears to be tonal.' No stress placement statement.
Only source Z'graggen (1980); retyped lexicon; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Has a phoneme chart and grammar notes under the name Vanembere and may mention accent, BUT Z'graggen 1980 (p. vii) and Pick 2020 (fn. 39) both say this material is Musar/Hember Avu, not Mokati -- open only to confirm the identity, not as a Mokati source.
